segments.text: Voters in New Hampshire have selected
their nominees to replace Democratic
Senator Jeanne Shaheen, who's not
seeking re-election. On the Republican
side, John Sununu defeated Scott Brown
in a battle of former US senators, one
from New Hampshire, one from
Massachusetts, interestingly.
Congressman Chris Pappas, who had the
backing of Senator Shaheen, prevailed in
the Democratic primary.
And in the state's race for governor,
Cindy Warmington, who ran unopposed,
will face incumbent Republican Kelly
Ayotte. And Cindy Warmington joins me
now. Cindy, congratulations on your
victory. Thanks for joining us. So, you
heard Nancy and I talking about the
president's remarks today that oil
prices, therefore gas prices, will not
come down until after the midterms. How
do you evaluate that?
>> Well, not surprising to me that
President Trump is making yet another
claim that he cannot back up,
unsubstantiated.
And fuel prices are really hurting the
people here in our state. Recently, I
was visiting at a farm where the cost of
diesel has driven up the cost of putting
crops into the ground, the cost of
getting them out of the ground, the cost
of transporting crops and dairy products
to the marketplace, and driving up the
cost for everybody in our state.
>> What about the trade war with Canada?
New Hampshire, I've been there many,
many times, has fond relationships with
Canada and integrated economic
relationships with Canada.
>> Yes, and being a border state, you know,
we have a lot of trade with Canada. And
with this this trade war that Trump has
started has been hurting tourism in our
state. We've already seen tourism down
by 30%, which is hurting our small
businesses. We've seen the cost of goods
go up, the cost of lumber that we need
for building houses, the cost of farm
products, equipment, feed,
the cost of diesel fuel. It This trade
war is really crushing the people of our
state. And we have a governor in Kelly
Ayotte who is completely unwilling to
stand up to Donald Trump and fight for
the people of New Hampshire. As
governor, I will stand up and fight for
the people of New Hampshire, making sure
that President Trump knows the damage
that his tariffs are doing to the people
of our state.
>> You invoked the name of Kelly Ayotte,
the governor, but most recent polls have
her ahead of you by at least 10
percentage points. This is an uphill
climb. I'm sure you'll acknowledge that.
Are you Are you relying only on the
atmosphere?
>> It's going to be a tough race. There's
no question. But Kelly Ayotte actually
has some of the lowest approval ratings
we've seen of any governor in more than
30 years. And everywhere I go across the
state, people are completely fed up with
the inaction of Kelly Ayotte's
administration. And all of the things
that she's doing that are actually
driving up costs for the people of our
state, putting in an education voucher
scheme, um jacking up the cost of
property taxes across our state, and
increasing premiums on the most
vulnerable of Granite Staters. People
are really fed up. They're ready for a
change. I'm ready to bring it to them.
>> Cindy, an issue that has persisted in
not only this race, but an earlier race
you made for governor in 2024 is your
history as a Purdue Pharma lobbyist.
Early in the 2000s,
before the state legislature, you said
that OxyContin was not subject to abuse,
was a miracle drug. You were clearly
parroting the party line, the company
line. How much do you regret that
advocacy then?
And how do you deal with this issue now,
which persists?
>> As I have said many times, Uh, I did
not, of course, know of Purdue Pharma's
fraudulent scheme back in 2002, but I
certain most certainly regret ever
having anything to do with Purdue
Pharma, given what we know now. Uh, I
have been profoundly uh, affected by
addiction in my own family, and uh, it
is an issue that I have spent a lifetime
working on. And I am convinced that the
people of New Hampshire recognize that
Kelly Ayotte is attacking me because she
is unable to defend her own record as
governor, that she is unable to defend
the fact that she has sent the cost of
health care and housing and school uh,
property taxes through the roof, that
our electric rates are some of the
highest in the country because of her
failed policies. I think the people of
New Hampshire recognize that Kelly
Ayotte has no record to run on.
>> Cindy Warmington, the Democratic nominee
for governor, great state of New
Hampshire, appreciate the time.
>> Thank you.
